original_question: For the inverse limit of the iterated natural degree-five alternating permutational wreath products, Eberhard asks for a finitely generated dense subgroup of subexponential growth.
reviewed_claim: The ordinary subgroup generated by one fixed compatible pair a,b in the full alternating rooted-tree inverse limit is finitely generated and dense, and its ordinary word balls for {1,a,a inverse,b,b inverse} have log cardinality divided by radius tending to zero.
checks: Alphabet is Fin 5 and A5 is its actual alternating permutation group. Wreath P is P^5 semidirect A5 by inverse reindexing, the natural five-point permutation action. The left-action convention changes stored root cycles, not the group or problem.

Level 0 is trivial and Level(n+1) is Wreath(Level n); levelProj deletes the deepest layer. compatibleSubgroup contains every compatible sequence in the full product, with no extra closed-subgroup or finite-support constraint. Its subtype AutTree is the intended inverse limit.

Every finite level is proved finite and is given its discrete topology. The group inherits the product/subspace topology. dense_of_surjective_levels directly uses open finite-coordinate neighborhoods, so Dense refers to the actual inverse-limit topology.

a and b are fixed compatible sequences. Density proves their same subgroup surjects on every finite level; it does not choose a different pair depending on the level. generatedSubgroup is ordinary subgroup closure, and the finite-generation endpoint uses {a,b}.

WordGeometry requires a finite symmetric generating set containing identity and exhaustiveness by its finite powers. Its ball is the actual finite-set power and volume its cardinality. The concrete wordGeometry is built on exactly generatedSubgroup with {1,a,a inverse,b,b inverse}. Thus no artificial sequence is substituted for word growth.

Including identity makes the nth power the ball of length at most n. Its cardinality is positive, so real-log defaults at zero cannot trivialize the limit. Radius zero has no effect atTop. SubexponentialGrowth is the literal Tendsto(log(volume n)/n,0).

generatedSection is the actual tree section in the same subgroup, with closure proved using finite words. root_sections_injective follows from the faithful decomposition of actual compatible sequences. Solution converts the proved section-word shortening to lengths in the concrete geometry and discharges the general counting theorem with actual representatives of all ball elements.

The counting criterion has explicit injectivity, coverage, and shortening hypotheses; each is supplied by a proof in Solution. It derives the analytic recurrence and logarithmic limit without assuming subexponential growth. The final endpoint has no remaining mathematical parameters.
scope_boundary: Qualitative subexponential growth only. No additional constant-200 or other explicit rate is claimed. The review identifies the inverse-limit tower and ordinary metric semantics; it is not an independent paper-level referee proof of every counting lemma.
